$comment: Runtime metadata the registry entry format does not carry.
`awesome-dsh-plugin` entries are probe output: url, name, category, description, and an optional tarball.
The list's own prober answers exactly one question — does the repository declare `dsh.bundle.patch` in
its package.json? — so `installable: true` says a bundle exists, not that it will run here.
That leaves three things a user cannot learn from the registry and the market cannot answer: what the
plugin exposes, what it needs installed, and which dsh line it was built against. This file carries
them. Nothing reads it yet; that is the point — it is the field set proposed for the entry format, kept
in the package so it can be adopted incrementally without breaking the existing consumers.
name: dsh-plugin-anything-bundle
requiresNotes: Nothing beyond Node. The tools shell out to `dsh` and `node`, both of which are already present wherever this plugin is installed. `plugin_anything_promote` additionally requires the `dynamicCordisRunner` service and does not register without it.
dshRangeNotes: dsh publishes no stable release. A range without a prerelease tag (^0.1.5) resolves to nothing, and a range is line-specific: this one does not admit 0.1.6-alpha.1.

tools.name: plugin_anything_probe
tools.purpose: Classify a target as a CLI, an HTTP API, or an MCP server, and gather evidence that it is actually callable. Reports `kind: mcp` as a stop condition.

tools.name: plugin_anything_inspect
tools.purpose: Gather what a target actually offers as normalised evidence: version, subcommands with verbatim help text, top-level flags. Collects facts and reports its own gaps; does not extract capabilities.

tools.name: plugin_anything_scaffold
tools.purpose: Write a bundle skeleton from the kit's templates. Existing files are never overwritten; unresolved placeholders become visible TODO markers.

tools.name: plugin_anything_compile
tools.purpose: Compile a Capability IR into plugin source. The backend reads capabilities rather than sources, so the same IR produces the same code whoever wrote it; it reports what it declined.

tools.name: plugin_anything_verify
tools.purpose: Run the kit's static gate over a bundle. Reports a failure rather than a pass when it cannot locate the gate.

tools.name: plugin_anything_install
tools.purpose: Install a bundle into a profile and confirm its layer composed, grepping the row id because a patch that matches no row only warns.

tools.name: plugin_anything_accept
tools.purpose: Run the acceptance tail — build, compose, boot, discover, invoke, present, replay — and return one verdict. A stage that could not run yields `incomplete`, never a pass.

tools.name: plugin_anything_package
tools.purpose: Produce the distribution artifact and compare it against the manifest's `files`, so a promised entry that is absent is reported rather than shipped.

tools.name: plugin_anything_promote
tools.purpose: Capture a live dynamic cordis package as source on disk so it can be converted into a real bundle. Writes an intermediate artifact, not a finished bundle.
tools.conditional: Registers only where `dynamicCordisRunner` is mounted — the dsh-web-app bundle provides it; dsh-base does not.

verified.note: What has evidence, and what does not. See docs/runtime-acceptance.md.
verified: installs, composes, loads, registers, and persists across restarts
the model lists all tools and calls plugin_anything_probe successfully
a presenter renders from a real logged tool/result
the bundle ships its own skill, discovered via createRequire
promote reads a real dynamic package created by cordis_define
unverified: no stable dsh release exists to test against
the promoted output has not been produced end to end without a human completing the source conversion

categoryRationale: `tools` — the plugin's output is tools. It compares with the entry format's other categories: `dev` covers development workflows, `skill` covers skill delivery, and this does neither.
